summary: AsteriaHealth: cascading stream stalls and out-of-order transcripts during morning peak — post-incident follow-up & customer credit request
description:
Issue summary:
During the customer AsteriaHealth's peak traffic window (07:00-08:30 UTC on 2026-03-10) we observed cascading streaming stalls and intermittent out-of-order transcript segments for conversational generation requests. Customers reported repeated partial transcripts followed by delayed segments that arrived out of sequence, and in some cases the stream terminated with a 502. The issue caused elevated error rates and duplicate downstream processing in Asteria's ingestion pipeline, producing measurable business impact for their live triage workflow.

Impact:
- AsteriaHealth observed ~18% of streaming sessions with stalls or truncations during the peak window.
- Several downstream jobs de-duped and reprocessed transcripts, increasing their compute costs and latency for clinical triage.
- Customer requested immediate credits for the affected window and a follow-up remediation plan.

Environment:
- Production, us-east-1 region, traffic routed through standard Redwood hosted API.
- Affected model families: redwood-open-7b-v2 (primary) and redwood-quant-7b-ggml (fallback).

Steps to reproduce (high level):
1) Customer sends long-form streaming chat with multi-segment function calls (~tokens 600-1200).
2) Under sustained parallelism (50-150 concurrent streams) during prefix-heavy workloads, streams experience stall followed by out-of-order chunk delivery.
3) Replaying captured requests from the time window reproduces truncated stream or delayed segment reordering when run at customer concurrency levels.

Observed signals / logs (representative):
- api-gateway: increased 502s and upstream reset logs correlated with spike at 07:04 UTC.
- serving-runtime: repeated per-request KV cache misses and spike in kernel-selection fallback logs to quantized variant at 07:03-07:12 UTC.
- autoscaler: transient pod churn as new GPU nodes came up, followed by immediate eviction events at 07:05 UTC.
- customer-facing logs: transcript fragments with non-monotonic chunk indices (e.g., chunk 5 arriving before chunk 3).

Initial mitigation taken:
- Applied short-term routing policy to pin AsteriaHealth requests to a stable pool (no quantized fallback) at 07:15 UTC.
- Increased autoscaler cooldown to reduce pod churn and disabled aggressive preemptive scale-down for the tenant pool.
- Coordinated with Asteria's engineers to temporarily lower concurrency and enable client-side reassembly tolerance.

Customer request:
- AsteriaHealth formally requested a service credit for the 1.5 hour impact window and a written post-incident summary and action plan.
steps_to_reproduce: Replay production request batches captured between 2026-03-10T07:00:00Z and 2026-03-10T08:30:00Z at similar concurrency (50-150) using redwood-open-7b-v2; observe streaming stalls and non-monotonic chunk delivery when autoscaler cycles nodes while kernel-selection falls back to quantized variant.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Autoscaler preemption caused rapid pod churn; during handoff sessions were reassigned to quantized fallback instances lacking warm KV cache, producing missing prefix state and chunk reordering.
Hypothesis 2: Session mux had a race during chunk reassembly when streams moved across instances; ordering metadata occasionally overwritten when backpressure caused retransmit of earlier chunks.
Evidence: Elevated pod_eviction logs coincident with spike in kv-cache-miss and kernel-selection fallback. Replays at scale reproduced reordering only when autoscaler was induced to cycle nodes.
Mitigations validated: pinning tenant to stable pool removed fallback behavior and reduced stalls; session-affinity guard in canary prevented reordering during induced pod handoffs.
Telemetry gap: need better per-tenant tracing for chunk indices and stronger alarms on kv-cache-miss rate crossing 10% threshold.
resolution_summary: Hotfix deployed to session mux to serialize chunk indices during pod handoffs; autoscaler cooldown increased for tenant pools; temporary routing policy pinned AsteriaHealth to stable pool until further rollout. Customer issued a 40% credit for impacted window. Post-incident report delivered to customer on 2026-03-13.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-11: session-affinity guard commit merged (runtime PR #5123) and deployed to canary cluster for soak testing.
2026-03-12: increased autoscaler cooldown from 30s to 180s for dedicated tenant pools; disabled aggressive preemptive scale-down flags for enterprise-tier pools.
2026-03-12: routing policy created to prefer non-quant fallback for AsteriaHealth until warm-cache heuristics are improved.
2026-03-13: final runbook updates added: instructions for immediate pinning of tenant pools, checklist for validating kv-cache warmness after node transitions.
Finance: credit of 40% applied to AsteriaHealth invoice for 2026-03-10 impacted window (finance ticket FIN-2026-83).

Owner: Maya Chen (Support) — Deliver final customer-facing postmortem and collect formal acceptance of credit amount (due date: 2026-03-16).
Owner: Platform PM (Liam Ortiz) — Review autoscaler default cooldowns and preemption policy for enterprise pools; propose config change (due date: 2026-03-30).
billing_action: Applied a 40% service credit for AsteriaHealth for the impacted 1.5 hour window; finance ticket FIN-2026-83 created and customer notified. Support to confirm credit appears on next billing statement.
related_incident_notes: INC-2026-03-10-07-asteria-streams: Incident timeline and initial postmortem draft linked in Confluence. Root cause determination points to interaction of autoscaler preemption + session mux race during pod handoff.
public_communication: Customer-facing incident summary drafted and shared with AsteriaHealth; no public status-page event required as impact was isolated to single tenant but documented for internal learnings.
